claims.text: Atomic size mismatch among constituent elements governs the premelting and melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Atomic size mismatch modulates local lattice strain.
Higher atomic size mismatch produces greater lattice distortion.
Greater lattice distortion weakens bonding at nanoparticle surfaces.
Weakened surface bonding lowers the energy barrier for premelting.
Nanoparticles with minimal atomic size mismatch have higher melting transitions.
Nanoparticles with minimal atomic size mismatch have sharper melting transitions.
A high-mismatch compositional series will exhibit significant lattice distortion relative to a minimal-mismatch series.
Increased atomic size mismatch enhances surface disorder.
Lattice strain and surface disorder reduce surface cohesive energy.
Reduced surface cohesive energy triggers premelting below the melting temperature of minimal-mismatch nanoparticles.
High-mismatch nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at lower temperatures than minimal-mismatch nanoparticles.
High-mismatch nanoparticles will display a more gradual melting transition than minimal-mismatch nanoparticles.
Minimal-mismatch nanoparticles yield low lattice distortion.
Surface effects dominate the relevant premelting and melting behavior of HEA nanoparticles in the 5–20 nm size range.
Oxidation, surface segregation, and phase separation can affect the proposed relationship and therefore must be minimized.

contradictions.description: The intervention says to vary nanoparticle composition to alter atomic size mismatch while simultaneously keeping overall composition constant. Unless 'overall composition' means only fixed stoichiometric ratios rather than fixed elemental identity, these requirements conflict.
